subsystems.name: Tensor compute array
subsystems.role: does the arithmetic — mostly multiply-accumulate operations — for neural network layers.

subsystems.name: On-chip memory hierarchy
subsystems.role: feeds data to the compute array fast enough to keep it busy.

subsystems.name: Data movement and control
subsystems.role: moves tensors between memory, the array and the rest of the system.

subsystems.name: Compiler and runtime
subsystems.role: turns a trained model into an efficient sequence of hardware operations.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the engine within a phone's or laptop's heat and battery budget.

buildSteps.title: Define the workload
buildSteps.detail: Study which neural-network operations dominate real apps — convolutions, matrix multiplies, attention — and set targets for throughput, latency and power.

buildSteps.title: Design the architecture
buildSteps.detail: Choose the MAC array size, dataflow (weight-stationary or output-stationary), memory hierarchy and supported number formats such as INT8 and FP16.

buildSteps.title: Write and verify the RTL
buildSteps.detail: Describe the design in a hardware description language and simulate it against reference models until every operator matches bit-for-bit or within tolerance.

buildSteps.title: Physical design and tape-out
buildSteps.detail: Synthesise the logic, place and route it, check timing and power, and send the final layout to a foundry as a mask set.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate and package
buildSteps.detail: The chip is made on an advanced logic process and packaged, often as part of a larger system-on-chip alongside CPU, GPU and memory.

buildSteps.title: Build the software stack
buildSteps.detail: Write drivers, a graph compiler and quantisation tools so frameworks like ONNX or TensorFlow Lite can map models onto the hardware efficiently.

buildSteps.title: Validate and tune
buildSteps.detail: Run real models, measure accuracy, speed and power, then iterate on scheduling, clocking and memory use to meet product targets.

prerequisites.why: fitting billions of transistors into a phone-sized power budget needs the latest process nodes.
these dataflows reuse data on-chip, cutting the memory traffic that dominates energy use.
running models in INT8 or INT4 instead of FP32 makes them several times faster and cooler.
the compute array starves without memory close enough to feed it every cycle.
without automatic mapping of models to the NPU, developers would have to hand-tune every layer.

pathway.milestone: NPUs shipping in flagship phones, tablets and PCs from several vendors
pathway.unlocks: fast, private features such as photo processing, speech recognition and live translation running locally.

pathway.milestone: NPUs in cars, cameras, wearables and industrial devices
pathway.unlocks: always-on sensing and control that does not depend on a network connection.

pathway.milestone: on-device generative AI models running entirely on the NPU
pathway.unlocks: personal assistants and image tools that keep user data on the device.

pathway.milestone: tightly coupled CPU–GPU–NPU designs with unified memory
pathway.unlocks: larger local models and continuous, low-power ambient intelligence.
